title: How would you migrate an application from Java 8 to Java 17, and what technical challenges would you face?
shortTitle: How do you migrate from Java 8 to Java 17?

s1_definition.profdef: Migration steps: (1) compile with Java 17 — fix compilation errors (removed APIs, illegal reflective access), (2) add explicit dependencies for removed Java EE modules, (3) update libraries/frameworks to Java 17-compatible versions, (4) handle strong encapsulation of JDK internals (java.base, java.lang.reflect — `--add-opens` flags), (5) leverage new features (records, sealed classes, text blocks, pattern matching, switch expressions). Challenges: removed `javax.*` modules, strong encapsulation breaking reflection-heavy libraries, `sun.misc.Unsafe` restrictions, Nashorn JavaScript engine removal, deprecated Security Manager removal, module system conflicts.
s1_definition.analogy: Migrating from Java 8 to 17 is like the bank moving from a 10-year-old building to a modern tower. Most furniture (code) fits, but: some old electrical outlets don't work (removed APIs), some doors need new keys (strong encapsulation), the cafeteria moved (Java EE → Jakarta), and some old equipment isn't compatible (library updates needed). Plan: test everything, upgrade one floor at a time.
s1_definition.oneliner: Steps: compile → fix removed APIs → add Jakarta deps → update libraries → handle --add-opens → adopt new features. Biggest challenges: JAXB removal, strong encapsulation, library compatibility.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Migration steps: (1) compile with Java 17 — fix compilation errors (removed APIs, illegal reflective access), (2) add explicit dependencies for removed Java EE modules, (3) update libraries/frameworks to Java 17-compatible versions, (4) handle strong encapsulation of JDK internals (java.base, java.lang.reflect — `--add-opens` flags), (5) leverage new features (records, sealed classes, text blocks, pattern matching, switch expressions). Challenges: removed `javax.*` modules, strong encapsulation breaking reflection-heavy libraries, `sun.misc.Unsafe` restrictions, Nashorn JavaScript engine removal, deprecated Security Manager removal, module system conflicts.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Migrating from Java 8 to 17 is like the bank moving from a 10-year-old building to a modern tower. Most furniture (code) fits, but: some old electrical outlets don't work (removed APIs), some doors need new keys (strong encapsulation), the cafeteria moved (Java EE → Jakarta), and some old equipment isn't compatible (library updates needed). Plan: test everything, upgrade one floor at a time.

**One line to remember:** Steps: compile → fix removed APIs → add Jakarta deps → update libraries → handle --add-opens → adopt new features. Biggest challenges: JAXB removal, strong encapsulation, library compatibility.

sections.s2_technical:
Migrating from Java 8 to Java 17 (LTS) spans several versions of change, so the approach is incremental and evidence-driven. First, inventory the code with `jdeps --jdk-internals` and the module/removed-API checks; the same Java EE/CORBA removals from Java 11 apply, plus more internal APIs are now strongly encapsulated under the module system (`--illegal-access` was removed in Java 17, so reflective access to internals now fails outright).

Second, upgrade build tooling and dependencies: compiler plugin `release` to 17, and bump libraries (especially bytecode-manipulating ones like older Hibernate, Lombok, Mockito) to Java 17-compatible versions. Third, adopt the new features where they help: records, sealed classes, pattern matching for `instanceof`, switch expressions, and text blocks all reduce boilerplate.

A banking example: a monolith on Java 8 is migrated by first making it compile and pass tests on Java 11, then on Java 17, fixing removed modules and reflective internal access at each hop, and finally refactoring DTOs to records. Senior nuance: migrate in hops (8 to 11 to 17) rather than one jump, run the full test suite at each hop, and treat library upgrades — not language changes — as the main source of risk.
sections.s3_banking: Problem — A Java 8 banking monolith had to reach Java 17 for LTS support, but a single jump risked breaking reflective library hacks and removed modules all at once. Fix: migrate in hops (8 to 11 to 17), running the full test suite at each step, fixing removed Java EE modules and strongly-encapsulated internal access, then adopting records and sealed classes.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Input: a list of migration issues discovered by jdeps and the test suite.

**Step 2.** Hop 1 — compile and test on Java 11: fix removed Java EE/CORBA modules by adding dependencies.

**Step 3.** Hop 2 — compile and test on Java 17: fix strongly-encapsulated internal access (no more --illegal-access) and bump incompatible libraries.

**Step 4.** Adopt new features: convert DTOs to records, use sealed classes and switch expressions where they clarify code.

**Step 5.** Each issue maps to a concrete action; the full test suite passes on Java 17.

```text
INFO: removed-module→add dependency; internal-access→supported API; old-library→bump
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ JAVA 8 → 17 MIGRATION CHALLENGES ═══

  Challenge                          │ Fix
  ───────────────────────────────────│──────────────────────────────
  Removed Java EE modules (JAXB)    │ Add jakarta.* Maven deps
  Strong encapsulation (reflection)  │ --add-opens JVM flags
  javax.* → jakarta.* namespace     │ Spring Boot 3.x handles this
  sun.misc.Unsafe restrictions      │ Use VarHandle instead
  Nashorn JS engine removed          │ Use GraalJS
  Library incompatibility            │ Update to latest versions
  Deprecated SecurityManager         │ Remove usage (Java 17 warns)

  ═══ NEW FEATURES TO ADOPT ═══

  Java 9:  Modules, List.of(), Optional.ifPresentOrElse
  Java 10: var (local variable type inference)
  Java 11: HttpClient, String.isBlank/strip, Files.readString
  Java 14: Records, switch expressions, NullPointerException messages
  Java 15: Text blocks ("""), sealed classes (preview)
  Java 16: Pattern matching instanceof, Stream.toList()
  Java 17: Sealed classes (final), enhanced pseudo-random generators
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Migrating Java 8 to 17 involves five steps: compile with Java 17 and fix errors, add explicit Jakarta dependencies for removed Java EE modules, update all libraries and frameworks to Java 17-compatible versions (Spring Boot 3.x, Hibernate 6.x, JUnit 5), handle strong encapsulation with --add-opens JVM flags for reflection-heavy code, and run the full test suite. The three biggest challenges are: JAXB/JAX-WS removal (add Jakarta dependencies), strong encapsulation breaking internal JDK API access (--add-opens or migrate to public APIs), and library compatibility (some older libraries don't support Java 17). After migration, adopt new features: records, text blocks, pattern matching instanceof, sealed classes, and switch expressions for cleaner, more maintainable code.
